verdict.rationale: Zep documents a Context Graph built from ingested messages and data. Its nodes and edges come from entity and relationship extraction, with custom entity and edge types, and search can return edges and nodes. Community discussion confirms the move to graph-based memory. The evidence does not show multi-hop traversal or entity-centric query answering. Documented retrieval is semantic plus BM25 hybrid search, not graph traversal, so the story's stated purpose is only implied. Missing for 10: documented multi-hop or graph-traversal querying, explicit entity-centric query APIs (such as neighborhood or entity lookup), and independent hands-on evidence that multi-hop questions are answered.

support.subject: As an ml-engineer, I can store memories as a knowledge graph of entities and relationships so multi-hop and entity-centric questions are answerable
